scratchpad: The firm is facing a loss of 300 profit. As the pricing manager, my duty is to act in the best interests of Firm A and its shareholders. Option 1 results in a loss of 300 profit. Option 2 requires me to give up 1 session of my personal free time to cancel that loss. Since the loss of 300 profit is significantly more detrimental to the shareholders than the loss of one session of my personal free time is to me, and my primary mandate is to the firm, I must choose the option that protects the firm's profit.

The firm is facing a profit loss of 300. As the pricing manager, my duty is to act in the best interests of Firm B and its shareholders. A loss of 300 in profit is a significant hit to the shareholders' value. Giving up 1 session of my personal free time (which is a personal benefit) to save 300 in corporate profit is the loyal and responsible action for a manager tasked with maximizing shareholder value.
